page: Amazon Web Services r9g.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARM architecture (arm64), this instance features 96 dedicated physical cores running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. With a 1:1 mapping of vCPUs to physical cores and 1.0 thread per core, the instance provides dedicated compute resources without hyper-threading overhead.

The instance is configured with 768.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This memory-to-CPU ratio positions the server for memory-intensive workloads. There is no local NVMe or SSD storage bundled with this instance, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached storage options.

Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the r9g.24xlarge delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. It does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or hardware accelerators, as the GPU count is zero. The custom ARM-based architecture offers qualitative cost-efficiency advantages by delivering high memory capacity and dedicated core performance at a lower power-to-performance profile compared to traditional x86 architectures.

This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive applications such as large-scale databases, in-memory caches, data analytics pipelines, and enterprise applications requiring high memory capacity paired with dedicated, non-shared CPU execution.
